title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The current generation, continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming. Key model IDs as of mid-2025:

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Current default Sonnet |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Most capable; also powers Claude Code Fast mode |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision. **Superseded by the Claude 5 family below as of mid-2026** — Haiku 4.5 is the only Claude 4-era model still in the current lineup.

---

## Claude 5 Family (2026) — Current Generation

Anthropic introduced a fourth tier above Opus in 2026: **Mythos**, reserved for frontier-class models, with **Fable** as the first publicly-released Mythos-class model. The lineup now spans four tiers:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest (still on the `4.5` line as of this writing)
- **Sonnet** — balanced default workhorse
- **Opus** — high capability at moderate cost
- **Fable / Mythos** — frontier-class, state-of-the-art on nearly all capability benchmarks

**Claude Fable 5** launched June 9, 2026 as Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, reaching general availability across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork on July 1, 2026 (export controls lifted June 30). It leads agentic-coding evaluations with independent testing reporting roughly 80% on SWE-Bench Pro, and is priced at $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens (2× Opus 4.8's pricing). It ships with conservative guardrails on high-risk domains (cybersecurity, biology) that trigger in under 5% of sessions.

**Claude Opus 5** followed on July 24, 2026 — Anthropic's fourth Claude 5 model release in under two months, reflecting a broader industry shift from blockbuster launches toward rapid, incremental releases. Opus 5 targets Fable-class performance at a fraction of the cost: it comes within 0.5% of Fable 5 on CursorBench 3.2 at half the cost, and surpasses Fable 5 on OSWorld 2.0 at one-third the cost, while doubling Opus 4.8's score on Frontier-Bench v0.1. Pricing held flat at $5 / $25 per million tokens, with Fast mode running 2.5× faster at 2× base cost.

**Key specs (Opus 5):** 1M-token context window, up to 128K output tokens, adaptive thinking on by default, a five-level effort setting, mid-conversation tool changes (beta), automatic safety fallback to alternate models (beta), and visual output generation.

**Current model IDs (as of August 2026):**

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest; still Claude 4-era |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Current default Sonnet |
| Opus 5 | `claude-opus-5` | Default Opus; 1M context, adaptive thinking |
| Fable 5 | (Mythos-class) | Frontier tier; also has an internal-only sibling, Mythos 5 |

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens (Opus 5, mid-2026)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use → Visual output generation
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → Four tiers with the addition of Mythos/Fable
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing; Opus 5 now approaches frontier-tier (Fable) performance at a fraction of Fable's cost
- **Release cadence:** Shifted from infrequent blockbuster launches to rapid, incremental model drops (four Claude 5 releases in under two months by August 2026)
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, adaptive/effort-tunable reasoning, and integration with external systems
